case_title: Union of India & Ors. v. Bodupalli Gopalaswami
statutory_provisions: Army Act, 1950 s. 52(f), s. 63; Pension Regulations for Army (Part I) Regulation 16(a)
trial_court_outcome: Dismissal from service with forfeiture of pension
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the Commandant of a supply depot, was charged with three offenses related to the management of a butchery. The first charge involved the acceptance of meat containing hearts, which were not acceptable parts of carcasses, as part of the dressed meat. The second charge was related to the failure to ensure that required stocks were maintained as reserve in the butchery. The third charge concerned the improper implementation of standard operating procedures for the butchery, resulting in passed animals not being segregated. The accused was found guilty of these charges, leading to his dismissal from service and the forfeiture of his pension. The High Court quashed the order forfeiting the pension, and the Supreme Court set aside the dismissal and substituted it with a lesser punishment of forfeiture of eight years of service for pension purposes and a severe reprimand.
